2_Introduction: The control device displays a JSC of 25.25 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.094 V and an FF of 75.8683%, tuning out a PCE of 20.9565%. For perovskite film, the solution concentration of Cs0.05MA0.08FA0.87PbI3.0 was 1.63 mol/L. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated onto the substrate at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. During the last 15 s of the second step, the anti-solvent (150 µL of chlorobenzene) was dropped in the center at a constant rate The substrates were immediately transferred to the hotplate and annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-concentration (1.63 mol/L) precursor solution of Cs0.05MA0.08FA0.87PbI3, incorporating a small Cs⁺ fraction to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor for enhanced phase stability, was deposited via a two-step spin-coating process where an initial 1000 rpm spread step ensured uniform wetting before a rapid 5500 rpm acceleration to thin the film, with the precisely timed introduction of 150 µL chlorobenzene antisolvent during the final 15 seconds critically initiating rapid nucleation by supersaturating the precursor solution and controlling solvent evaporation dynamics. The immediate transfer to a 110°C hotplate for 15-minute annealing then promoted the growth of dense, pinhole-free crystalline grains by driving off residual solvent and facilitating the reorganization of the PbI₆ octahedral framework, a process where the mixed A-site cation composition (Cs⁺, MA⁺, FA⁺) suppressed detrimental hexagonal phase formation and mitigated ion migration, thereby reducing bulk defect density and non-radiative recombination pathways to yield improved carrier lifetimes. This optimized crystallization protocol directly enhanced charge extraction at the interfaces, minimizing voltage losses and improving fill factor by fostering a continuous, uniform morphology with efficient percolation pathways for photogenerated carriers, ultimately resulting in a champion device performance with a VOC of 1.094 V, a JSC of 25.25 mA/cm², an FF of 75.8683%, and a PCE of 20.9565%.
